newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's Labor hails Blair victory.
newsitem.headline: Australia's Labor hails Blair victory.

text.p: Australia's Labor Party, now in the political wilderness after 13 years in power, on Friday hailed the British Labour Party election victory and turned to Tony Blair for some guidance.

Australia's Labor politicians said Blair's "great victory" was in part a result of the lessons he learned from the Australian Labor Party, which Blair reportedly says is his model for a free market, centre-left government.

According to media reports, Blair took political advise during the recent British campaign from former Australian Labor prime minister Paul Keating. A former Keating official also worked in the Blair camp.
"There's a deal that we've got to learn from Tony Blair's election victory...," said Labor opposition leader Kim Beazley.
Beazley said Blair's victory was a result of his ability to restructure the British Labour Party to make it relevant to the British people after 18 years in opposition.
"And he learned a lot from us, as he would acknowledge himself...," said Beazley.

Australia's Labor abandoned its ideological baggage in the 1980s and 1990s to become a centrist party. Blair also moved British Labour to the centre and exorcised the ideological demons which frightened voters in the 1992 British election.
Australia's Labor government was thrown out of office in 1996 on a similar scale to Labour's victory in Britain.
The British election was a mirror of the Australian poll -- a tired, unpopular government versus a fresh opposition -- but with the political parties reversed.

"What I think we can learn from him (Blair) is that very strong sense of community that he pushed through, underpinning all his policies -- community values, community responsibility, community opportunities," Beazley said.
"We're going to pick up a fair bit of that over the next couple of years -- that seems to be the right way to go and he's developed it to a considerable extent," he said.
Australia's conservative prime minister also congratulated Blair and said his counterpart John Major never stood a chance.

"I congratulate Mr Blair on an outstanding victory and send commiserations to my good friend John Major, who fought a courageous personal campaign in quite impossible circumstances," said John Howard.
